full_judgment:
4. The trial Court upon hearing the parties decreed the suit in part directing the petitioner to pay Tk. 19,599.50 as prompt dower. Tk. 15,000/- for the maintenance of the plaintiff at the rate of Tk. 5,000/-per month and to pay Tk. 18,000/- for the two minor daughters at the rate of Tk.300/- each per month for a period of 2 years from the date of filling of the case and thereby decreed in total an amount of Tk. 52,999/50. 

 5. Against the said decree, the petitioner preferred an appeal and the lower appellate court affirmed the decision of the trial court but modified the decree by decreeing the entire dower money by increasing the decretal amount to Tk. 72,999.00. 

 6. A learned Single Judge in revision affirmed the appellate judgment and decree. 

 7. Mr. Md. Amir Hossain learned Advocate-On-Record appearing for the defendant-petitioner submits that the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division acted wrongly in affirming the decree of the entire dower money passed by the lower appellate court when the marriage tie between the plaintiff and the defendant is still subsisting although the petitioner pronounced talaq by swearing an Affidavit on 11. 4. 90 but the same was not a valid talaq in the eye of law as no notice to the Chairman of the Union Council was served as required under Section 7 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961. 

 8. Admittedly the plaintiff and defendant were married on 11.11.83 by a Nikahnama, Ext. 1 Wherein the entire dower was fixed. Two daughters were born in wedlock. The plaintiff was divorced on 11.4.90 by the petitioner by pronouncing talaq by an affidavit sworn before a Magistrate and the copy of the same was sent to the Nikah Registrar as per provision of Section 6 of the Muslim Marriage and Divorce (Registration Act). 1947. Consequently, the marriage tie between the parties was terminated from the date of affidavit Ext. A dated 11.4.90. It is admitted by the petitioner that he pronounced talaq by affidavit. Ext. A, but no notice under Section 7(1) of the Ordinance was served to the Chairman. The defendant did not willfully serve notice to the Chairman as provided under Section 7 of Ordinance, 1961. It is on record that the divorce was registered in the concerned Kazi office in accordance with Section 6 of The Muslim Marriages and Divorces (Registration) Act 1974. There being admission by the petitioner that he gave talaq to the respondent by swearing an affidavit before the Magistrate and that he sent the affidavit to the Nikah Registrar as per Section 6 of the said Act of 1974 the talaq is accepted by the petitioner. Consequently the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division acted rightly in affirming the decree of the lower appellate Court with regard to the entire amount of dower both prompt and deferred. Section 7 (1) of the Ordinance provides for giving of notice of talaq to the Chairman and a copy thereof to the wife and provides for punishment for contravention and this law overrides any other provision of any other law. But there being clear intention to divorce by the Affidavit on the part of the petitioner and the same having been disclosed and produced before the lower appellate court by the petitioner himself, the petitioner cannot take advantage of his own wrong and cannot claim the benefit of non-service of notice by him to the Chairman. He is bound by his admission. Payment of dower being obligatory as per Nikahnama the wife is entitled to the same on talaq. In the facts of the case the decision has been correctly arrived at. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division committed no illegality in affirming the decree of the lower appellate court.
